About The Academy
Headteacher Welcome
Welcome to The Wellington Academy. It is a privilege to lead a school where every young person is supported to grow with confidence and purpose. Everything we do is shaped by our commitment to helping students be ambitious, inquisitive, and independent, as these three values guide the learning experience and the opportunities we provide.
We encourage ambition by helping students set high goals for themselves in all areas of school life. We nurture inquisitiveness by creating an environment where questions are valued, curiosity is encouraged, and learning is active and engaging. And we promote independence so that students develop the resilience, responsibility, and self-belief they need for future success.
As a proud member of the Ascend Learning Trust, we are strengthened by a shared vision for excellence across all schools within the Trust. The motto “Together we Belong, Believe, Become” reflects what we strive to achieve each day. Our students belong to a safe, supportive community; they believe in their ability to achieve; and they become young people who are prepared for the next stage of their lives.
Our aim is to ensure that every student is known, valued, and encouraged to make the most of every opportunity. Through inspiring teaching, rich experiences beyond the classroom, and strong pastoral support, we work together to help each individual grow academically and personally.
Thank you for taking the time to learn more about our Academy. I warmly invite you to visit us and see first-hand how our values of being ambitious, inquisitive, and independent shape the culture of our school and the achievements of our students.
Together, we belong. Together, we believe. Together, we become.
Mrs Hannah WhitakerHeadteacher Email: headteacher@twa.ascendlearningtrust.org.uk
Ascend Learning Trust
We are proud to be part of Ascend Learning Trust, a forward-thinking family of schools working together to deliver exceptional education and opportunities. Together we belong, believe, become is more than a motto—it’s a shared commitment to nurturing every learner and empowering every educator. As part of this Trust, we benefit from strong collaboration, leadership, and a clear vision for success.

pageCache.text:
Welcome to our 6th Form
The Wellington Academy 6th Form is unique. As well as excellent grades in a range of subjects in both A-Level and BTEC options, we offer an outstanding range of extra opportunities that you will not find anywhere else.
The ethos of the 6th Form is ‘limitless aspiration’; we spend a lot of time ensuring that students not only succeed to the best of their ability in subjects of their choice, but they leave us at the end of year 13 having had the opportunities to experience programmes designed to both enhance their future choice prospects, and also develop as a young adult ready for the world beyond school.
The 6th Form has grown in strength each year. Our results improve year on year, and the number of opportunities increase also. Student feedback is very positive, with all students rating the department as being very supportive and effective in this support. Whilst our numbers are increasing each year, we are still a small enough 6th form to be able to offer personal support and guidance and bespoke curricular plans. A common theme in feedback is the ‘family atmosphere’.
Students leave us to greater things at the end of year 13. Last year for example, every single student left to a destination of their choice, be it higher apprenticeships, university, or employment; over 70% of students chose university as their destination and these choices included Russell Group universities.
We hope you have a look through the rest of the department pages; if you would like to come in for a look around or experience the school in action, please do not hesitate to get in touch.
Like what you hear so far? Why not check out some of the subjects you could choose by visiting our Courses and Curriculum Page.
Dave Bissington Head of 6th Form

6th Form Courses and Curriculum
The Wellington Academy 6th Form Curriculum
At Wellington we offer a range of both A-Levels and BTECs. Students would typically chose three subjects, but a number do opt to start with four. Some BTECs are on offer as a ‘double’, and if this option is chosen then that subject would take account for two of the three possible choices.
It is also perfectly possible to mix BTECs and A-Levels. For example a student may opt to study Double Health & Social Care (Diploma) with A-Level Psychology. Alternatively they may chose single Health & Social Care (extended certificate), with A-Level Psychology and BTEC Child Development for example.
Any student not achieving a grade 4 or higher in English Language or Maths GCSE or equivalent is required by law to re-sit these until a grade 4 is achieved. We offer a resit programme to support this.
For a quick rundown on all courses offered, please visit our main curriculum page.
If you have any questions or queries please contact us.
Entry Criteria
Entry to Wellington 6th Form is by application form and interview. We interview each applicant to ensure that they have had appropriate guidance in terms of subject choice and we are the right choice for them. Whist we accept students on a case-by-case basis, the general criteria are:

Information, Guidance, and Support (IAG) runs weekly for all students, and each student is allocated a tutor who they keep in regular contact with through the week. Careers Education
Our Careers Programme Vision And Strategy
Careers Vision Our careers programme reflects the wider careers vision of Ascend Learning Trust, encouraging pupils to Challenge, Aspire and Network and to develop the skills and experiences they need for a successful future.Strategic Priorities 1. To equip all pupils to challenge themselves and be challenged to develop employability skills, independence, courage and confidence through our integrated careers programme. 2. To support all pupils to aspire to a bright future that is well-informed and transcends barriers by being inquisitive about options and opportunities, accessing up-to-date LMI, career-planning tools, advice and well-developed career plans. 3. To broaden and strengthen all pupils’ networks by providing opportunities to meet a diverse range of industry professionals, helping them raise their ambitions and discover the full range of pathways available.
The programme is built around the Eight Gatsby Benchmarks that have been well-researched and commended by the Government.
We run a number of careers and work-related learning events throughout the school year. At appropriate times we also run trips to Further Education Colleges, Universities and Higher Education and Apprenticeship fairs as well as to subject-focused careers events.

Pastoral Support
The pastoral care at The Wellington Academy is driven by a student-centred approach through pivoting and adapting to meet the needs of the students day-to-day.
In maintaining and monitoring systems at the Academy, the role of the tutor is key; tutors are the first point of contact for parents and students and will be able to identify issues before other members of staff. It is the job of the tutor to get students ready to learn in the morning and ensure that they have everything they need and logging accordingly on their conduct cards and Arbor house points.
Punctuality and attendance are vital to students’ success. Tutors are also expected to check students’ phone pouches every morning and their uniform.
The pastoral team work to ensure that staff, students, and families are supported. Interventions, support plans and additional academic and pastoral strategies may also be implemented to support the behaviour/pastoral needs of the student.
Each year group has a non-teaching year group leader with a Head of Key Stage overseeing them and working with the tutors to lead the year group and set high expectations for attainment, progress and conduct.
All of the above is overseen by the AHT for Behaviour & Culture.

Parent FAQs
Please make sure you ring as early as possible, ideally before 8.30. You will need to ring on each day that your child is unwell. For all year groups please contact the main academy telephone number 01264 405060, choose option 1 and leave a message.
Please call the main Academy number on 01264 405060.
The first port of call should always be with your child’s tutor who will endeavor to reply to you within 24hrs of your message being received. If for any reason you do not receive a response please contact your child’s student manager
The core subjects of English, maths and science will set at least one 30 minute piece of home learning for all students in KS3 and KS4 every week.
The non-core subjects will set at least one 30 minute piece of homework for all students in KS3 and KS4 every fortnight. For accelerated groups, the homework task will be more challenging and require greater student independence.
As you will be aware, we monitor both academic achievement and attitude to learning on a regular basis. Reports are issued through the Parent Portal. If you need support using this, please contact your child’s student manager.
Term dates and holidays are published on our website under The Academy tab, Calendar & Term Dates.
Please send a note with your child which you have signed. This needs to be given to their teacher at the beginning of the lesson they need to leave. The teacher will then sign it to confirm they are ok to leave.
Teaching staff are teaching from 8.40 – 3.00 and will aim to respond to your query outside of these times.
All staff have access to email and are happy to receive queries through this method of communication.

ParentPay Information
In Spring 2016, the Academy introduced a cashless environment. This ensure’s a safer, more efficient environment for our students and staff.
Please note we will no longer accept cheques.
All parents are allocated a ParentPay account and, if they require, a PayPoint card. These accounts and cards are used to pay for school lunches, trips, music lessons and much more.
ParentPay
ParentPay offers you the freedom to make secure, online payments whenever and wherever you like, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
You will have a secure online account, activated using a unique username and password; you will be prompted to change these, and to keep them safe and secure. If you have more than one child at the Academy, you can create a single account login for all your children.
Making a payment is straightforward and ParentPay holds a payment history for you to view at a later date. Once you’ve activated your account you can make online payments straight away.
Other ParentPay benefits include:
ParentPay website includes lots of helpful user videos to answer any queries.
Parent Pay Log in
Pay with cash using PayPoint
Please contact our finance department, if you wish to use the PayPoint facility for school meals. You will be issued with a card to make cash payments for school meals at local PayPoint stores. The first card is free of charge; however, any lost or damaged cards will be charged at £3 each. Payment cards take about two weeks to arrive but we are able to issue a barcode letter as an interim measure.

If you wish to pay for a trip via PayPoint, please request a barcoded letter from our finance department. This will carry a unique barcode which will allow you to make cash payments for this specific trip, at your local PayPoint store.
PayPoint payments are recorded by ParentPay and can be seen by logging into your ParentPay account and viewing your payment history online.

Other Useful Information
Internet Access– for those who do not have internet access at home, access to ParentPay will be provided at the Academy. Alternatively, public computers with internet access are available at both Ludgershall and Tidworth library and Ludgershall council office. Second Login – a separate login can be provided for each parent/carer. This can be provided on request. Daily Meal Limit – a daily limit can be set on a student’s meal account, limiting the amount they spend on food each day. All purchases can be viewed within your ParentPay account. Please contact our finance department if you wish to set a limit. Frequently Asked Questions – a ParentPay FAQ section will soon be available on the Academy’s website.
If you experience any difficulties or problems using ParentPay please email finance.twa@ascendlearningtrust.org.uk or call 01264 405060 and ask for the finance department, who will be able to offer support and advice.
Your support in using ParentPay helps the Academy enormously, thank you.

Curriculum at The Wellington Academy
At The Wellington Academy our core values of Ambitious, Inquisitive and Independence are the three pillars of our curriculum and underpin all that we do.
The Wellington Academy Curriculum provides all students with skills and knowledge; enabling them to demonstrate academic success but also the ability to flourish in the wider world and become ambitious for themselves. To this end we provide a broad and balanced curriculum designed to enable our students to access a wide range of subjects and develop a deeper understanding and love of these subjects.
Through our design and delivery of the curriculum we seek to engage students, encouraging them to challenge themselves and ideas, enabling them to become inquisitive learners. We endeavour to provide our students with the learning environment and tools that enable them to develop personally as well as academically to ensure that they become independent thinkers and develop resilience.
The curriculum enables students to embody our values and be ambitious, inquisitive and independent, preparing them for the next stages of education, employment or training.

Careers Education, Info, Advice and Guidance
IAG and work-related opportunities are an important part of the curriculum both embedded in our teaching and learning and through additional activities such as work experience, the assemblies programme, and our Values curriculum. It is of the utmost importance that all young people are encouraged and supported to move towards a working life which is right for them; will be enjoyable and provide economic well-being. This is done through the provision of relevant and impartial careers advice and access to meaningful work-related opportunities. More details can be found on our website.
Enrichment
At The Wellington Academy, we believe that regular participation in extra-curricular activities is just as important as excelling in academic subjects. According to numerous studies, students who take an active part in extracurricular activities have better leadership skills, enhanced team working skills and higher levels of sympathy than their peers. Extra-curricular activities enable students to develop skills that will benefit them for life. For example, joining the football club can improve hand-eye coordination and teamwork skills, attending a drama class will harness their creativity whilst developing public speaking skills. Other benefits include:
• Improved self-esteem
• Exploration and a broader perspective
• Wider social network with actual rather than virtual interactions
• Time management and responsibility
• Greater opportunities for success
All students are encouraged to participate in at least one extra-curricular activity per week, selected from a broad and diverse menu, including sports clubs, theatre, music, creative arts or learning a new language to name but a few. A full list of what is offered is published termly on the school website.
